# Results — Study 788 (Overnight / Intraday Tug of War)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
the Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019) cross-sectional **"tug of war"**: stocks with high past
**overnight** (prev-close → open) returns keep earning overnight (persistence) while
**reversing** intraday (open → close), and vice-versa. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `d3f2054309d3` (panel Open+Close), `357fd262912f` (Close only).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,146** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Decomposition | exact night/day identity via `quantlab.decompose`: `r_overnight = Open/prevClose − 1`, `r_intraday = Close/Open − 1` (Open and Close share the same daily adjustment factor, so the split survives total-return adjustment) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the **trailing-21-day mean overnight return known at the close of `t−1`** (one `shift`); top 30% minus bottom 30%, equal-weight; measure the day-`t` overnight leg and (separately) intraday leg of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold the overnight+intraday legs of `t` (the overnight leg is capturable — you enter at the close of `t−1`, the instant the signal is known). The costed timer charges the overnight-capture round trip (enter close, exit open) as 2 legs × 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on each daily leg-spread series; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled top-vs-bottom book legs; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership**
list of names that are liquid mega-caps *today*. Feeding it to a backward-looking
panel omits the delisted / de-rated names, so the cross-sectional magnitudes here are
an **upper bound** (biased upward). The qualitative tug (a positive overnight leg, a
negative intraday leg on the H-L spread) is the robust finding; the exact bps are not.

## The headline — legs of the trailing-overnight-sorted H-L spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% spread (n = **4,125** days), per leg:

| leg of the H-L spread | mean/day | NW(10) *t* | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **overnight** (persistence) | **+3.71 bps** | **+4.62** | +4.40 |
| **intraday** (reversal) | **−2.39 bps** | **−2.36** | −2.27 |
| close-to-close (≈ on + id, the net) | +1.32 bps | +1.06 | — |
| **tug = overnight − intraday** | **+6.10 bps** | **+4.59** | — |

High-past-overnight names keep earning **overnight** (persistence, *t* = +4.62) and
give it back **intraday** (reversal, *t* = −2.36) — the two legs pull in opposite
directions, exactly the Lou-Polk-Skouras tug of war. Decisively, the legs roughly
**cancel close-to-close** (+1.32 bps, *t* = +1.06, not significant): the tug is a
within-day redistribution, not a net close-to-close premium. Gross overnight-spread
Sharpe ≈ **1.09** (before any cost).

**Pooled book legs (Welch).** Top book overnight +6.76 bps vs bottom +3.05 bps
(Welch *t* = +2.12); top book intraday +1.65 bps vs bottom +4.04 bps (Welch
*t* = −1.16) — the same asymmetry from the pooled angle.

## Placebo — is the persistence a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-overnight sort but read each day's forward overnight legs from a
**column-permuted** panel (signal → outcome link broken, each day's cross-sectional
distribution preserved), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed overnight spread | **+3.71 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.001 bps (0.597) |
| p (share of permutations ≥ observed) | **0.00000** (0 / 1,000, ≈ 6σ out) |

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | overnight spread | NW *t* | intraday spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,991) | +2.99 bps | **+4.32** | −3.90 bps | **−3.21** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +4.38 bps | **+3.11** | −0.97 bps | −0.62 |

The **overnight persistence** leg holds in both halves (*t* = +4.32 then +3.11). The
**intraday reversal** leg is strong early (*t* = −3.21) but fades to insignificance in
the recent half (*t* = −0.62) — the reversal side of the tug has weakened, while the
persistence side has not. (An honest sub-period read, not a claim of decay in the
overnight leg, which is if anything larger recently.)

## The timer — can you capture the overnight persistence leg?

The tradable version enters the H-L book at the close of `t−1` and unwinds at the
open of `t` to bank the overnight leg — turning the whole 2×-NAV book over twice a
day. Cost = 2 legs × 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day; the short book pays 50 bps/yr
borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | round-trip cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +3.71 bps | 4.14 bps | **−0.43 bps** | −0.51 | −0.13 | −1.1%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +3.71 bps | 20.14 bps | **−16.43 bps** | −19.49 | −4.82 | −41.4%/yr |

The overnight leg is worth **+3.71 bps/day gross**, but capturing it means crossing
the spread four times a day on a 2×-NAV book. Even at a **1 bp** one-way cost the
round-trip friction (4.14 bps/day) already **exceeds the entire gross edge** — net
−0.43 bps/day, *t* = −0.51. At a realistic 5 bps it is deeply negative. The signal is
real; the paycheck is not.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent overnight-demand factor; the
overnight leg loads +`tug`, the intraday leg −`tug`. No network.

| world | overnight NW *t* | intraday NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`tug = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.19** (sd 1.03), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** | — |
| planted (`tug = 0.0020`, seed 788) | **+10.51** | **−11.15** |

The detector never fires on the null and recovers a planted tug cleanly. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The trailing-overnight sort produces a **positive overnight
  leg** (+3.71 bps/day, NW *t* = **+4.62**) and a **negative intraday leg**
  (−2.39 bps/day, NW *t* = **−2.36**) on the H-L spread — the Lou-Polk-Skouras tug of
  war, clearing **t ≥ 2** on the real tape in both directions, holding across both
  sub-periods (overnight *t* = +4.32 / +3.11), with a clean 20-seed synthetic control.
  The legs roughly cancel close-to-close (*t* = +1.06), so this is a within-day
  redistribution, not a net premium. **Survivorship caveat travels on this axis**: the
  current-membership mega-cap panel biases the magnitudes upward.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Capturing the overnight leg turns a 2×-NAV book over twice
  a day; the round-trip friction exceeds the entire +3.71 bps/day gross edge at a mere
  **1 bp** one-way cost (net −0.43 bps/day, *t* = −0.51) and is −41%/yr at 5 bps. A
  real signal you cannot get paid for.
